problems.title: Work versus merge sort
hints: Network work is O(n log² n).
problems.solution: Ratio ≈ 5.2: bitonic does over 5× the comparisons at this size, so it's used for blocks that fit on chip, with merging beyond.

problems.title: Pair indexing
problems.statement: Thread t's pair at distance j is i = ⌊t/j⌋·2j + (t mod j) and i + j.
hints: Pairs at distance j come in groups of 2j.

problems.title: Barriers you can drop
problems.statement: 512 keys, 256 threads (8 warps). Steps with distance j involve pairs within the same warp's data when the pair indices of a warp's lanes stay within 64 consecutive keys.
problems.solution: Steps with small j can use __syncwarp (or registers and shuffles); only the large-distance steps need __syncthreads.

problems.title: Merge rounds
problems.statement: Sort 2²⁴ keys: blocks sort runs of 2,048, then pairwise merges.

parts.prompt: Bytes moved by the merge rounds (FP32 keys, read + write each round)?

problems.solution: 13 rounds, 1.62 GiB: the rounds, not the comparisons, dominate the time.

problems.title: Data independence

options: The comparison sequence doesn't depend on the data

problems.solution: Every thread knows its pair at every step; only the swap direction depends on data (a select).

problems.title: Bank conflicts in bitonic
problems.statement: Lanes 0–31 at distance j = 32 read words i = ⌊t/32⌋·64 + (t mod 32): for t = 0..31, i = 0..31, and partners 32..63.

parts.prompt: Conflict degree reading the i words?
At j = 64, the partner words i + 64 for i = 0..31: degree?

problems.solution: Both are 32 consecutive words: conflict-free. Conflicts appear in other steps where lanes' i values are spread with even strides; padding or swizzling fixes them.

problems.title: Stable or not

options: No: equal keys can be reordered by the network

parts.prompt: How do libraries make it stable when needed?

problems.solution: Not stable; append the original index as a tiebreaker.

problems.title: Registers instead of shared memory
problems.statement: Each lane holds 4 keys; steps with distance below 4 stay in a lane's registers; distances 4–127 use shuffles across lanes (128 keys per warp).

parts.prompt: For a warp sorting 128 keys, total steps?
Steps done entirely within a lane's registers (j ∈ {1, 2})?

problems.solution: The in-register steps need no communication at all; the rest use shuffles, still no barriers or shared memory.

problems.title: Choosing a sort

parts.prompt: Many independent lists of 64 floats (top-k per query)

problems.solution: Radix for big integer arrays, networks for small segments, merge sort for comparison-only keys.
